verdict.rationale: Clerky documents a Partner API, but it covers only Delaware C-Corp formation (create a document set, render forms, submit values, poll state), and signing still happens on Clerky. Its OAuth authentication is marked 'coming soon'. The remote MCP server is live behind OAuth, but the probe describes its tools as read-only. The UI offers far more, including SAFEs and convertible notes, stock plans, hiring paperwork, IRS filings, bank applications and 40+ attorney products, none of which the API exposes. missing for 10: API coverage of SAFEs/notes, equity/stock plans, hiring, IRS filings, bank applications, attorney products, collaboration/review workflows, API-side signing, generally available authentication, write-capable MCP tools.
